title: Rotate Square Submatrix Clockwise
description:
You are given an `m x n` integer matrix `grid`, integers `row`, `col`, `k`, and `turns`.

Consider the `k x k` contiguous square submatrix whose top-left corner is at `(row, col)` (covering rows `row .. row + k - 1` and columns `col .. col + k - 1`). Rotate **only** this `k x k` submatrix clockwise by `90` degrees exactly `turns` times, while leaving every cell outside the submatrix unchanged.

Return the resulting `m x n` integer matrix.
constraints: 0 <= row <= m - k and 0 <= col <= n - k
hints: Four 90-degree rotations return the submatrix to its original orientation, so first reduce t = turns % 4.
Copy the grid and map each relative offset (dr, dc) inside the k x k window directly to its target position based on t in {0, 1, 2, 3}.

examples.explanation: The bottom-right 2x2 submatrix [[5,6],[8,9]] rotates 90 degrees clockwise into [[8,5],[9,6]], leaving row 0 and column 0 untouched.
Rotating the entire 2x2 matrix twice (180 degrees) reverses both rows and columns.
Because 4 turns is a full 360-degree rotation, the matrix remains completely unchanged.
